title: Dad Jokes
subtitle: One or several corny, boring jokes.

items.text: Dad Jokes

items.speaker: Oliver Fog
items.text: Well, that's everything done, more or less... Let me check my work schedule.

items.speaker: Oliver Fog
items.text: Good. Then I can clock off now.

items.speaker: Oliver Fog
items.text: It's not that noticeable during the daytime, but as soon as night falls, this forest becomes excruciatingly quiet.

items.speaker: Oliver Fog
items.text: Hm... I hate places that are this silent.
It reminds me of the fog I have to immerse myself in almost daily.
Where even my shouts and cries for help are swallowed up by this bedevilled fog.
Waaaaah!!!

items.speaker: Oliver Fog
items.text: What's this? It's too dark to see clearly ...

items.speaker: Oliver Fog
items.text: Critters! And they're attacking!
Squeeeee!!!

items.speaker: Oliver Fog
items.text: There's even more of them than I'd feared ...

items.speaker: Oliver Fog
items.text: And there's no kind of natural shelter around... If I stay put, they'll eventually surround me.

items.speaker: Oliver Fog
items.text: Fortunate that I absorbed quite a bit of fog while working this afternoon. It should still be usable...

items.speaker: Oliver Fog
items.text: Hah... So this my reward for all that hard work?

items.speaker: Oliver Fog
items.text: No, I shouldn't think like that.

items.speaker: Oliver Fog
items.text: But work's the reason I ended up in this mess.

items.speaker: Oliver Fog
items.text: It looks like there are fewer enemies in that direction... I think I just might break through that way.
A dense fog pours out from above his umbrella, quickly enveloping the surrounding area.

items.speaker: Oliver Fog
items.text: Phew... That was a narrow escape, all thanks to the fog... At last it seems there aren't as many critters around here.

items.speaker: Oliver Fog
items.text: It's too dark now, and with the fog, I couldn't even make out what kind of critters were attacking me...

items.speaker: Oliver Fog
items.text: I need to rest for a bit now... I'll figure out how to get out of here once I catch my breath.
Fogwalker, are you alright, my young friend?

items.speaker: A Knight
items.text: Are you truly so surprised to see someone here, Fogwalker?

items.speaker: Oliver Fog
items.text: ...Mr. Knight!

items.speaker: A Knight
items.text: Did you think me a Dullahan? Or else what other vile thing did you see as to elicit that reaction on seeing someone here.

items.speaker: Oliver Fog
items.text: I thank you for using the word "surprised" instead of "panicked" regarding my reaction.

items.speaker: A Knight
items.text: I have no interest in shaming your reaction, Fogwalker.

items.speaker: Oliver Fog
items.text: Well then, Mr. Knight, what brings you here?

items.speaker: A Knight
items.text: Someone had the sudden impulse to play the part of a stone in the forest. See? Someone's disguise is quite perfect, is it not? Even your keen eyes failed to detect someone's presence amid the moss and trees.

items.speaker: Oliver Fog
items.text: Don't you think it would have been even stranger if I had managed to notice you there?

items.speaker: A Knight
items.text: Because the night is so dark?

items.speaker: Oliver Fog
items.text: Mr. Knight, this kind of banal joke is what we commonly refer to as a "dad joke."

items.speaker: Oliver Fog
items.text: I haven't heard a line as terrible as that since my father passed. And I'd rather I never heard such a thing again...

items.speaker: A Knight
items.text: Please forgive me. Someone didn't mean to stir up memories from your past. Someone deeply regrets having upset you so.

items.speaker: Oliver Fog
items.text: Come now. It was a long time ago. I don't really care much about it anymore, anyway.

items.speaker: A Knight
items.text: In that case, perhaps you might tell someone more about your father? Someone is quite interested in the previous Fogwalker.

items.speaker: Oliver Fog
items.text: You want me to tell you about my father?

items.speaker: Oliver Fog
items.text: I'd rather not. I can't think of a single thing worth mentioning about him.

items.speaker: Oliver Fog
items.text: He was an ordinary man, and the most ordinary Fogwalker... A Fogwalker who died in the fog.

items.speaker: Oliver Fog
items.text: And a failure of a father.

items.speaker: Oliver Fog
items.text: He hardly ever spent any time with my mother and me. Every single day, if he wasn't busy working, he was studying the arcane. And it was only when discussing arcanism that he would display a demeanor alike to an arcanist.

items.speaker: Oliver Fog
items.text: He spent his whole life studying and striving to push the arcane techniques of the Fog family forward, hoping to adapt them to the fog we now face in the modern era, but ultimately, it led him to his demise.

items.speaker: Oliver Fog
items.text: Ironic, isn't it?

items.speaker: Oliver Fog
items.text: I can scarcely remember what he looked like anymore. The only thing about him that left any sort of lasting impression on me were those few "dad jokes" he made around the dinner table.

items.speaker: Oliver Fog
items.text: Terrible, tasteless jokes.

items.speaker: A Knight
items.text: But he was a Fogwalker, and there was only one Fogwalker in all London.

items.speaker: Oliver Fog
items.text: People have attached a great deal of import to the title "Fogwalker," but in my opinion, a Fogwalker is not much different from a manure scooper.

items.speaker: Oliver Fog
items.text: Devoting yourself or even sacrificing yourself for the sake of your so-called responsibilities... there is nothing more foolish in the entire world.

items.speaker: Oliver Fog
items.text: I'll never live my life the way my father did. He was bound by the title "Fogwalker," but I won't let that happen to me.

items.speaker: A Knight
items.text: You admire your father greatly. Someone can feel it.

items.speaker: Oliver Fog
items.text: I do not...

items.speaker: Oliver Fog
items.text: When I was a child, I wanted to become a Fogwalker too, so yes... maybe then I admired my father greatly.

items.speaker: Oliver Fog
items.text: But things are different now.

items.speaker: Oliver Fog
items.text: It's only because he used to...
Wooooo!!!

items.speaker: Oliver Fog
items.text: Damn it! How did these critters ever catch up with me?
Dark shadows rush out from the depths of the forest, encircling the area before there's time to react.
Yet more shadows emerge from the forest depths, like smoke spewing from factory chimneys, thick and relentless.

items.speaker: A Knight
items.text: It appears we've found ourselves in something of a predicament.
TO BE CONTINUED ...
